## Government Prioritizes Domestic Chips

The government has moved to institutionalize preferential purchasing of domestically-produced semiconductors for national security infrastructure facilities. This strategic initiative is part of a broader effort to strengthen eight key industries including semiconductors, biotechnology, and defense. The government is also establishing a new export strategy finance fund to expand export support mechanisms. These measures reflect growing recognition that semiconductor competitiveness is essential to economic security and long-term growth sustainability in an increasingly competitive global environment.

## BOK Hikes Rates to 3.25%

The Bank of Korea's monetary policy committee raised the benchmark interest rate by 0.25 percentage points to 3.25% on November 26th, marking the third consecutive rate increase in the second half of this year. This aggressive tightening came despite broader economic headwinds, as policymakers prioritized price stability over growth concerns. The central bank simultaneously delivered a stunning revision to its economic forecasts, projecting growth of 3.9% for this year and 4.1% for next year—the strongest showing in 17 years. This represents a dramatic upward adjustment driven primarily by the semiconductor sector's exceptional performance, which is now expected to offset traditional downward pressures on the economy.

## Semiconductor Surge Reshapes Forecasts

Korea's semiconductor industry has emerged as the dominant driver of economic recovery, fundamentally altering the Bank of Korea's outlook for the coming years. The robust semiconductor export performance is expected to generate spillover effects throughout the economy, supporting consumer spending and overall demand recovery. Core inflation remains elevated at 2.8%, prompting the central bank's proactive monetary tightening. The BOK's decision to raise rates reflects confidence that semiconductor-led growth will be strong enough to withstand higher borrowing costs without derailing the expansion. Consumer prices are expected to rise 2.4% next year, up 0.1 percentage points from previous estimates, though the central bank believes this remains manageable within its inflation-targeting framework.

## US Tariff Threats Target Korea

The Trump administration has signaled it will maintain the 15% tariff ceiling on Korean goods negotiated last year while simultaneously threatening additional levies on semiconductor manufacturers specifically. American officials have cited what they describe as excessive government intervention in Korea's semiconductor industry, particularly regarding the Honam semiconductor cluster development. The United States has announced plans to impose "overproduction tariffs" on major trading partners, raising concerns about renewed trade tensions and potential inflation acceleration. These tariff threats pose significant risks to Korea's export-dependent economy at precisely the moment when semiconductor momentum is gaining strength.

## Stock Markets Rally on Stability Fund Hopes

Domestic equity markets surged sharply on November 27th, with the KOSPI index rising 204.47 points or 4.34% to close at 4915.68, reclaiming the 4900 level for the first time in three trading days. The KOSDAQ index jumped even more dramatically, gaining approximately 8% as investor sentiment improved. Foreign investors returned as net buyers for the first time in three months, purchasing 1.1256 trillion won on the KOSPI—their largest single-day purchase since early September. Expectations that the government would expand the market stabilization fund provided crucial support, with some analysts projecting the fund could grow from its current 10.76 trillion won to between 20 trillion and 40 trillion won. Individual investors, however, continued selling aggressively, offloading 1.7746 trillion won despite the broader market advance.

## Physical AI and Robotics Gain Momentum

The global artificial intelligence sector is shifting its focus from generative AI toward "Physical AI"—systems that can perceive and navigate physical environments to perform real-world tasks. Chinese electric vehicle manufacturer Xiaopeng has announced plans to begin commercial deployment of humanoid robots starting next year, with eventual transition to home use within one to two years. Korean robotics companies are intensifying competition in manufacturing automation, mobile humanoids, and AI-based cognitive control technologies to capture early market share. The AWS re:Invent conference scheduled for late November will prominently feature Physical AI and robotics as major technology domains, signaling the sector's growing importance to global corporate strategy and investment.

## Taiwan Forecasts 13% Economic Growth

Taiwan's economy is projected to expand 13% next year—the fastest growth rate in 48 years—driven by massive semiconductor industry expansion centered on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation. This exceptional forecast reflects the global surge in artificial intelligence infrastructure investment and the critical role Taiwan plays in supplying the chips that power AI systems worldwide. TSMC and its peers are expected to generate enormous capital spending and employment gains that will ripple throughout Taiwan's economy and create multiplier effects across the broader Asia-Pacific region.

## Residential Property Market Pressures Mount

Rising property values are creating unexpected challenges for ordinary homeowners, with one-home residents in areas like Wangsimni and Dangsan now facing comprehensive property taxes for the first time. Public apartment values exceeding 1.2 billion won are triggering comprehensive property tax obligations previously concentrated in Gangnam-area residences. The share of multi-property owners among total residential real estate holders has fallen to its lowest point in over eight years, while the percentage of South Koreans owning at least one residential unit has reached a record high. This divergence reflects tax-motivated selling by multi-property investors combined with increased owner-occupancy purchases by first-time homebuyers facing affordability pressures.

## Government Expands Public Housing Supply

The government announced plans to significantly expand public housing supply in the Seoul metropolitan region, targeting 56,000 units for 2027—roughly double the recent five-year average. Public rental apartment application timelines are being accelerated from one year pre-occupancy to two years and six months, bringing forward application opportunities for prospective tenants. The government is extending unfilled unit purchase commitments to private development sites in regulated zones for the first time, and expanding unfilled apartment purchases to non-regulated metropolitan areas. These measures aim simultaneously to address housing affordability concerns and stimulate private sector construction activity that has flagged amid policy uncertainty.

## For Investors and Citizens

The economic outlook balances genuine opportunities against meaningful risks. Semiconductor stocks remain compelling given 4.1% projected growth and strong export momentum, though tariff threats from the United States could quickly undermine these gains. The stock market rally reflects genuine fundamental improvement, but individual investors should recognize that foreign capital remains notoriously fickle and can reverse quickly. Interest rate increases to 3.25% will make mortgage borrowing more expensive for property purchasers while improving returns for savers and conservative investors. Those considering real estate purchases should act carefully given rising property values and increased tax obligations, while prospective tenants may benefit from accelerated public housing timelines and expanded supply. The critical variables to monitor include United States tariff implementation, semiconductor export trends, and whether the government's housing supply expansion actually delivers units at affordable prices for average households.
headline: Semiconductor Boom Drives 4.1% Growth, BOK Raises Rates to 3.25%
